comparison: Perfect agreement on ProtSSN architecture and design rationale (C5, C22-C26, C64-C65). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the methodological framework well-described and supported, with no concerns raised about the approach itself.

Both address the new benchmark datasets (C29-C31, C69-C70, C75-C81). OpenEval finds them well-documented and supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty due to concerns about sparse mutation coverage, unclear mutation distribution, and potential redundancy in assays.

Perfect agreement on ablation study results (C41-C46). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the systematic evaluation of design choices well-supported, with peer reviewers appreciating the breadth and clarity of the analysis.
Perfect agreement on robustness to folding methods (C48-C51). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the comparison of folding strategies compelling and well-supported with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on training data and setup (C71-C73). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the methodological details clearly stated and appropriate, with initial peer concerns addressed in revisions.

Significant disagreement on performance claims (C6-C7, C32-C33, C35, C38-C40). OpenEval finds comprehensive support across benchmarks, but peer reviewers express uncertainty due to missing comparisons with top-performing methods (EVE, GEMME) that reportedly outperform ProtSSN, and similar performance to SaProt after revisions.

Partial overlap on bootstrapping consistency (C39-C40). OpenEval finds evidence of consistency supported, while peer reviewers accept the robustness analysis after revisions without specific challenges to these claims.

Partial overlap on virus exception and MSA comparisons (C53-C54). OpenEval finds the exception well-explained with citations, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about MSA-based method comparisons, questioning potential data leakage and zero-shot learning definitions.

Minimal overlap on MSA-based method comparisons (C52, C55). OpenEval finds comprehensive comparison supported, while peer reviewers' concerns about missing top-performing methods and similar SaProt performance create uncertainty about the claimed advantages.

Minimal overlap on structure vs. language model performance (C36). OpenEval supports the inference that large language models don't match structure-informed methods, while peer reviewers' concerns about missing comparisons and similar SaProt performance suggest this claim may be overstated.
